fields.ley: rich, normal, thin or dead: the natural density, from the Ley Line map
fields.danger_tier: the region's tier on the shared ladder (local, regional, realm, world, mythic); it does not scale with the player
fields.eras: campaign eras the entry applies to; missing means all three

regions.name: The Dwarven Empire
regions.terrain: high mountains, cold valleys, a forested western shore on the Gulf of Aldir
regions.ley_note: Thin in the west around Mordun, rising to rich along the eastern peaks where the Great Line runs.
regions.summary: The north of the continent, ruled from the mountain city of Dun Aldun. Brutal winters, closed gates and the best steel in the world.
regions.travel: Outsiders come in by sea through Mordun or overland from Mendle. Mountain passes close in winter.
hazards: Rulan Gaan cultists on the eastern roads

regions.name: The Torogh Highlands
regions.terrain: a great lake under a wall of snow peaks
regions.ley_note: The northern convergence of the Great Line. Tradition puts the Source Font in the peaks above the loch.
regions.danger_note: The lake shore is local. The high peaks are mythic: nobody who goes looking for the Source Font comes back the same.
regions.summary: Fishing boats, merchant tales and the mountains where seven mortals became gods.
regions.travel: Roads run west to Mendle and the human kingdoms; the peaks have no roads at all.

regions.name: The Gulf of Aldir
regions.terrain: a sheltered gulf with a pirate archipelago in the middle
regions.summary: Calm water, rich cargoes and the Scullcrossed Islands squarely on the route. Profit for the bold, a grave for most.
regions.travel: The Trein to Mordun run is the busiest shipping lane on the map.

regions.name: The Kingdoms of Man
regions.terrain: the temperate western lowlands: farmland, rivers, sea cliffs
regions.ley_note: Far from the Great Line. The west runs on crystal.
regions.summary: The human west: Trein's lit streets, Asania's marble towers and Wrenspire's machines, all leaning on stored power or clever gears.
regions.travel: Good roads from Trein south through Asania to Wrenspire and east to Cyrel.

regions.name: The Kingdom of Cyrel
regions.terrain: lake country, farmland and logging forest, rising to the Badlands escarpment in the east
regions.ley_note: A Badlands branch current reaches west under Kingswood and Convila.
regions.danger_note: Local in the heartland, regional along the Asanian front and the Badlands line.
regions.summary: A fortress capital and three sister cities, fighting Asania to the west and the Badlands to the east, and the elves of Brynwyr over the forest.
regions.travel: Roads link Cyrel, Eriane, Kingswood and Convila; Bastion sits on the eastern road.
hazards: Brynwyr wardens on the forest edge

regions.name: The Badlands
regions.terrain: shattered mountains, dry basins, dead trees, sand
regions.ley_note: The Badlands convergence, where Ghondiir died, is one of the richest points on the Great Line.
regions.summary: The Dragon King's corpse-country. Three tribes, endless border war with Cyrel, and the strongest magic on the continent under the most dangerous ground.
regions.travel: No roads, only tribal routes, wells and the old Adlmyr road. Water is the currency of passage.

regions.name: Brynwyr
regions.terrain: old forest on the south-western peninsula, sea cliffs and harbors
regions.summary: The high elves' forest realm and fleet. Closed, proud, and at war with Cyrel's loggers over every tree.
regions.travel: Humans enter by invitation or by trespass. The treaty stones at Kingswood mark the line.

regions.name: Sa'ja'een Bay
regions.terrain: a warm bay of glowing water and coral towers
regions.summary: Bioluminescent water, coral towers, silver mist at dusk and creatures that sing at night.

regions.name: The Sea of Kujuur
regions.summary: Rough water around the southern islands, sunken treasure stories and goblin trade fleets.

regions.name: Bashrat Island
regions.terrain: hot swamp, mist, mangrove and singing wildlife
regions.summary: A muggy swamp island between the bay and the sea, home to frogfolk, chaos-toads, naga and lizardfolk, and a market everyone eventually hears about.
regions.travel: Goblin ships from Kadragar and elven ships from Brynwyr.

regions.name: Ikto Isle
regions.terrain: a small rocky isle past the Mi Cho Rapids
regions.ley_note: The Great Line passes close on its way out to sea.
regions.summary: A quiet island cut off by the rapids, home of the Benzaiten Monastery.
regions.travel: Only boats that know the Mi Cho Rapids, which means the monks' own.

regions.name: The Eastern Forests
regions.terrain: deep forest and lakes between the Badlands mountains and the sea
regions.ley_note: The Great Line runs through them south-east to the sea.
regions.summary: Old forest beyond the Badlands. Almost nobody comes back with a description.
regions.travel: Through the Badlands or by sea; the wood elves allow neither.

regions.name: Etryona
regions.terrain: a green island behind city walls, across the Kyrana Channel
regions.summary: Green walls, prism towers and a society where Ley crystal is money, rank and addiction.
regions.travel: The Kyrana Channel is hostile water; Obirykan ships trade with Petrakyra and few others.

regions.name: The Fjallagracht Lands
regions.terrain: snow, ice and mountain on an island across the Dire Sea
regions.ley_note: A branch current from the northern convergence runs out to the Gurdalur Stones.
regions.summary: A frozen island of hard clans whose lives run on the calendar of the Gurdalur Stones.
regions.travel: Across the Dire Sea in the short summer.

regions.name: The Dire Sea
regions.terrain: cold, deep northern water between the continent and Fjallagracht
regions.summary: The Fjallagracht clans named it for what it takes. Where the Ley branch runs beneath it, the sea throws up Ley squalls: storms with glowing fog that sour compasses and spells alike. Crystal reefs grow on the seabed along the current, and the clans' longships cross only in the summer weeks the Gurdalur calendar marks as safe.
regions.ley_note: The branch current from the northern convergence runs under the sea to the Gurdalur Stones. Ley under water does not circulate cleanly.
regions.travel: Fjallagracht longships in the summer windows; nobody else on purpose.
regions.origin_note: Named on the map only; extrapolated from the Ley Line map (Vanta asked, 2026-10-21).

regions.name: Faerie
regions.terrain: a brighter, stranger mirror of the world
regions.summary: Two queens, a muse and a hunter. Beauty and danger are one thing there, and time is unreliable.

regions.name: The Nine Hells
regions.terrain: nine layers from Avernus to Nessus
regions.summary: Law, contracts and promotion by treachery. See canon/cosmology.md.

regions.name: The Abyss
regions.summary: Hunger, chaos and the will to unmake creation. See canon/cosmology.md.
